object_description: compact three-storey volume slightly offset from the residential slab, with windmill clusters around an atrium
design_condition: the compact volume is geometrically offset from the neighbouring residential slab so that it forms a harmonious composition with the existing buildings and a new sequence of outdoor spaces follows the split between primary and secondary use

positive: The project finds a balanced approach to a context marked by two divergent visions of settlement
The compact three-storey building offset from the residential slab creates a harmonious composition
The treatment of the listed building shows a precise interpretation of the existing structure
A new sequence of outdoor spaces naturally follows the allocation of primary and secondary use
An open entrance hall links the main entrance and the secondary school playground in front
Keeping the southern part of the site free of further structural interventions proves very advantageous
A clear spatial organisation and rational structure enable a precise distribution of uses
Four clusters are arranged windmill-like around an atrium staircase on the two upper floors
Two classrooms and two group rooms form a cluster and provide a flexible learning landscape
Movable room dividers in the group rooms enhance this flexibility
The simple floor plan typology allows clusters to be formed across three to four units
The central library location makes sense as it is used by day school and elementary school too
The location of teacher areas, multi-purpose rooms and day school on the ground floor makes sense
The distribution of use across the entire site seems sensible and appropriate
Prefabricated facade elements and large glazing follow the inner logic with pleasant proportioning
Concrete elements and wooden windows combine into a deliberately abstract facade
A relatively compact volume with a simple insulation perimeter
Good internal thermal mass means hardly any risk of overheating
Construction costs are in the medium range thanks to the compact building and restrained interventions
The project achieves a high level of architectural quality
negative: The internal path network is only offered via an existing bottleneck or peripherally along the street
The opportunity to specify the design of the outdoor spaces is missed and statements remain vague
The daylit access areas are restricted in flexible use by the required checkrooms
Clusters across three to four units lose their stringency
The day school and multi-purpose rooms remain very vague and schematically formulated
Access and spatial proportioning of the multi-purpose rooms have not been resolved
The day school should respond more precisely to catering, play and recreation needs
The distribution occasionally results in long distances
Repositioning the janitor apartment impairs the optimisation of the room distribution
The expression seeks a relationship with the neighbouring residential slab and fails to appreciate what is there
The design turns away from the existing qualities of the complex in its expression
The window arrangement does not appear tested in terms of use or need for openness
The interplay of mineral surfaces and hard materials leaves a cool impression
Acoustic and functional measures are expected that will not stand up to the image of abstraction
The desire for abstraction does not fully meet the requirements of today's learning environments
On closer inspection the design remains somewhat schematic
